keyPoints: Use the HTML <video> tag with the source file specified via the src attribute or a nested <source> tag.
Add the autoplay attribute so the video begins playing automatically once the page loads.
Example: <video src="clip.mp4" autoplay controls></video>.
modelAnswer:
Use the video tag and specify the clip source and type with a nested source tag. Set width and height if a fixed display size is required. To make the clip start when the webpage loads, use autoplay instead of controls. The muted attribute may be added because browsers commonly restrict unmuted automatic playback. For example:

<html>
<body style="text-align: center">
  <video width="500px" height="500px" autoplay muted>
    <source src="fifa-win.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  </video>
</body>
</html>

The video tag loads the clip, autoplay starts it as the webpage loads, width and height set its size, and the source tag identifies the MP4 file. When autoplay is used, normal play, pause, and volume controls are not provided unless the design adds a separate control arrangement.

keyPoints: JavaScript adds interactivity and dynamic behaviour to an otherwise static HTML page.
It can respond to events, validate form input, and update page content without reloading.

Example:

changes the paragraph text when the button is clicked.
modelAnswer:
JavaScript makes an HTML page dynamic and interactive. It is embedded in a script tag and can display output, respond to an event, show an alert, perform calculations, and change page content or styles. An event is an action sensed by the program, and event-based code runs a function in response. For example:

<html>
<head>
  <script>
    function msgSure() {
      alert("Are You Sure???");
    }
  </script>
</head>
<body>
  <input type="button" onclick="msgSure()" value="Be Sure" />
</body>
</html>

When the button is clicked, the onclick event calls msgSure and displays the alert. Similar JavaScript can use document.write or a style property to update what the user sees.
